The ice maker on my Jenn-Air refrigerator stopped working so I watched a couple YouTube videos and to learn about all possible issues. The water line and inlet valve were working so the ice maker was the issue. I found the part number and called a local store that wanted $109 + tax for the part. I found the comparable part on Amazon and even with overnight shipping it was about half the cost.

The replacement included a control arm and two wiring harnesses but I reused my old ones. The install took about 5 minutes and I was back in business for Friday night cocktails!

I'm writing this review the day of install so I can't speak for the long-term durability but it started making ice within 3 hours and I feel like Bob Vila. Amazon rules! Cheers

Note there is a cut-out notch in the fill tray that I had to remove for my fridge.  Be careful as the fill tube may move in your fridge.  Mine pushed back into the fridge when I installed the ice-maker causing water spilling in the freezer. The bail was not attached properly when shipped.  I had to figure this out.  The only instructions that came with this had to do with setting the fill-level. There was one part left over- I have no idea what it's for.  It's working so far but based on the lack of attention to detail, I don't have high hopes it will be the last ice-maker I buy.

Soon after receiving this ice maker I installed it in my fridge. It made two batches of ice and froze up. I removed it and noticed that the outside plastic piece with all the fingers on it was bowed out and encased in ice. I thawed the icemaker and started comparing it to the original. I noticed that the finger nearest the water inlet housing was hung up underneath the housing. On the original icemaker, this finger was cut off so it couldn't get hung up. I called the supplier, told him what I found, and he sent me another one. In the mean time I decided to try to fix the first one. I cut off the finger nearest the water inlet housing so that it matched the original. I also put a bead of type 1 clear silicone adhesive under the outside plastic housing where it contacts the mold. This was to make sure it was securely bonded. After waiting a day for the adhesive to set up, I re-installed the icemaker. It started working fine. I waited a few days to make sure it wasn't going to fail again, then returned the second one they sent me unopened. The only problem I noticed was that about half of the ice cubes we're hollow. I have never seen that before but decided I could live with that. Everything was ok for about three weeks, then it froze up again. I called the supplier back and he sent me a third icemaker. I haven't installed it yet. I'm going to modify it like I did the first one and hope for the best. Maybe this one will be ok.

However, the ice detecting lever it came with is too short and can't sense when I have too much ice. If I leave it on, it will overflow. I threw the old parts away before I realized that. Dang! Now, I have to shut off the ice maker manually when there's enough ice and turn it back on when we need more ice. It's a pain. A lesson I'll never forget!

You need to scavenge parts (electrical cables, mounting flanges, water hose clip) from the old unit and cut a hole for the water inlet in the plastic hose mounting. I now have ice cubes again! I was afraid I would need to pay $150 plus parts to fix it. I called up the person who has fixed my washer and dryers for me, and he recommended I just buy a third party ice maker, and they usually go bad after 10 years.

It was relatively easy to replace. Better directions would have helped. I kept on comparing the old one to the new one, and used parts from the old one as needed to make the new one work. I was afraid it was not working, but I just needed to be patient.

What I could have done better:

1. Take photo(s) before disassembly. This would have made assembly easier.
2. Find and watch YouTube video.
3. Have bowl for screws out earlier.
4. Remove everything from freezer - dropped screws do happen.

We bought a Whirlpool fridge that came with a different filter (I think it was PUR) and we hated it! The water trickled out so slowly it was almost a joke. But we assumed it was a default of the fridge, not the filter. When we decided we needed to change out the filter, Amazon directed us to this Everydrop filter, saying it was the new version that was recommended. I noticed in the product summary that it claimed to filter more water per minute than the PUR. So we went ahead and got it and we couldn't be happier! We realized that the original slow water trickle was not the fridge, but the filter. This one gives a pretty steady flow; we aren't standing at the fridge forever now for a simple glass of water.

The water comes out kind of cloudy, from little bubbles in the filter process, but the cloudiness goes away within seconds. I was concerned the filter may not work as well, since it was filtering water faster, but a couple of people in the family actually get sore stomachs from unfiltered water here, so we know when the filters aren't working. There are no sore stomachs with this filter so we are very happy with the results.

When I first installed the filter, it took way more than the typical 5 gallons to have break the filter in. The water was full of micro-bubbles and the taste was not good until a good amount of water had been wasted. After the initial break-in period, the water from the dispenser was fine. 3 months after purchase, however, the taste suddenly turned a little metallic and it seems like the filter has lost its effectiveness.

A few months ago, my replacement light came on my fridge advising that it was time to replace my water filter, which is always dreaded because the manufacturer items can cost upwards of $30 bucks a pop. The size and shape of the water filter appears to be identical to the one I pulled out of my fridge. It was easy to install- screwed right in. The directions say to run 3-4 gallons through it, which I did. Still had a weird taste to it, so I ran a few more gallons through (no fear, I didn't waste 8 gallons of water- I put it in the flower beds to water.) That did the trick, and the water tastes just fine now- no discernable difference from the filter I had before, when it was still in its peak. The water definitely tastes much better now than it did yesterday, with my outdated water filter I was trying to make "stretch". For the money, this item is a definite win, and I will no longer have to compromise water taste quality due to reluctance to take out a second mortgage to pay for a new water filter. As a disclaimer, I did receive this water filter in exchange for a fair and unbiased review. I had never heard of this brand, but it's an item we all need (or at least all of us that have a fridge with water filter), and I figured "why not give something a shot that isn't going to cost an arm and a leg". That said, when the time comes that I need to purchase another replacement, I will be buying this brand and item again. To serve the same function as the costlier
